nodes.title: STEP 3 - Encode and align AV clocks
widgets_values:
## Step 3 — Feed the matching input-audio window into H3

The VHS loader exposes the full source soundtrack on every requeue. **Overlap Audio Window** uses the current overlap metadata and loaded frame rate to slice the exact audio time range matching this 73-frame model window.

The first synthetic overlap receives leading silence, later windows reuse the same source-audio overlap, and the final padded frames receive trailing silence. The aligned segment is encoded and passed to **H3 Source AV Prepare** with `audio_mode = lock`, so the model receives the real source audio while generating video and cannot rewrite it.

nodes.title: STEP 2 - Build an overlapping H3 window
widgets_values:
## Step 2 — Build the model window

The first window receives repeated leading context. Later windows receive the real tail carried from the previous source batch.

For the balanced preset:

- Model window: **73 frames**
- Shared overlap: **17 frames**
- New source frames: **56 frames**

The last short window is padded by repeating its final real frame.

nodes.title: STEP 1 - Load the source video
widgets_values:
## Step 1 — Load video and choose a preset

1. Upload the source video in **Load Video**.
2. Leave `frame_load_cap` at **0** so VHS can stream the complete file.
3. Start with **H3 Near 41 (39 / 5)**.

The preset sends stride **34** to the native VHS Batch Manager. VHS recognizes that native node and automatically requeues every chunk until the full source is done.

`format` stays at **None** so VHS does not discard the short final batch.

STEP 4 - Learned latent upscale
widgets_values:
## Step 4 — Upscale the video latent

The aligned AV latent is separated. Only the video stream enters the learned 2× latent upscaler.

The upscaled video is then restored into the original aligned AV container so the refinement sampler receives valid synchronized video/audio streams.

widgets_values_named.text:
## Step 4 — Upscale the video latent

The upscaled video is then restored into the original aligned AV container so the refinement sampler receives valid synchronized video/audio streams.

nodes.title: STEP 4C - Restore Upscaled Video into AV Latent
STEP 5 - Low-denoise refinement
widgets_values:
## Step 5 — Refine each overlapping window

The sampler runs the original low-denoise refinement after learned latent upscale.

Defaults retained from the source workflow:

- Steps: **5**
- Denoise: **0.20**
- Sampler: **SA Solver**
- Seed: fixed

Keeping denoise low helps adjacent windows remain close before overlap blending.

nodes.title: STEP 6 - Blend and save
widgets_values:
## Step 6 — Blend and save

After decoding, the output node compares the two processed versions of every shared frame and applies the selected blend ramp.

It holds only the small overlap tail, emits every source frame once, removes final padding, and tells VHS when the stream is complete.

The final **Video Combine** still receives the untouched full soundtrack directly from **Load Video**. The windowed copy is used only to drive H3.

## Using Prompt Embeddings

Prompt embeddings (supported since [ComfyUI#15697](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15697)) add reusable style tokens to your prompt. Download one or more embeddings from the folder above into `ComfyUI/models/embeddings/`, then reference one in the prompt text with the `embedding:` prefix and the filename without its extension, for example:

`embedding:minimaxh3_art_is_explosion`

Using an embedding is optional and the template runs fine without one.
